observation.visible_scene: A wide, muddy-brown waterfall pours over a rocky ledge into a churning pool, framed by dense green foliage on both sides. A white pedestrian bridge spans the top of the cascade, and a slender tree trunk stands at the right edge. The scene is a static landscape shot with continuous water motion.
visible_changes: The column of turbid brown water keeps falling down the rock face throughout the excerpt; its overall shape and position persist while the surface texture constantly re-forms.
Bright white foam streaks and rivulets on the face of the cascade shift and reorganize frame to frame, indicating turbulent downward flow rather than a single moving object.
A plume of white mist/spray at the base of the falls swells and recedes, its outline changing between frames.
The pool at the lower left shows swirling white foam patches that move and reshape over time.
The bridge, rocks, tree trunk, and surrounding vegetation remain fixed in the same image positions across all frames, so the apparent motion is in the water, not the camera.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the muddy, high-volume flow (rainfall, upstream release, etc.) is not visible.
Conditions upstream beyond the bridge and downstream beyond the pool are not shown.
Whether the flow rate is increasing, steady, or decreasing over a longer timescale cannot be determined from this short segment.
uncertain_details: Any very slight camera drift is not distinguishable from the moving water; the framing appears essentially fixed.
The exact boundary between falling water and standing rock is partly obscured by spray and foam.
